figures.text: Fig. 1 Characterization and structural analysis of mastoparan-S. A Characteristics of mastoparan-S. B Helical wheel projection of mastoparan-S. C Three-dimensional structural models of mastoparan-S generated using the PEP-Fold3 server; surface representation is provided. D Circular dichroism (CD) spectra of mastoparan-S (40 μM) were obtained in sodium phosphate buffer and bacteria membrane mimicking environments such as 30 mM SDS and 50% TFE

Antimicrobial activity of mastoparan-S and magainin 2 peptide against various gram-negative and gram-positive bacteria
Minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of peptides and antibiotics against Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolated from patients with otitis media in the Chonnam National University Hospital

Fig. 2 In vitro evaluation of the antimicrobial activity and cytotoxicity of mastoparan-S. Time kill kinetics of mastoparan-S at 1 ×, 2 ×, and 4 × MIC against A S. aureus and B P. aeruginosa. C Hemolysis of peptides against sRBCs. Cytotoxicity of peptides against D RAW264.7 cells and E HaCaT cells. Data are presented as mean ± SEM. Statistical significance was determined using an unpaired two-tailed Student’s t -test (* p ≤ 0.05, ** p ≤ 0.01, *** p ≤ 0.001)

In vitro evaluation of the antimicrobial activity and cytotoxicity of mastoparan-S. Time kill kinetics of mastoparan-S at 1 ×, 2 ×, and 4 × MIC against A S. aureus and B P. aeruginosa. C Hemolysis of peptides against sRBCs. Cytotoxicity of peptides against D RAW264.7 cells and E HaCaT cells. Data are presented as mean ± SEM. Statistical significance was determined using an unpaired two-tailed Student’s t -test (* p ≤ 0.05, ** p ≤ 0.01, *** p ≤ 0.001)

Fig. 3 In vitro anti-biofilm activity of mastoparan-S compared with the control peptide magainin 2 against A S. aureus and B P. aeruginosa . C Comparison of MBIC 50 values of mastoparan-S and magainin 2 against S. aureus and P. aeruginosa . D Biofilms of S. aureus and E P. aeruginosa were treated with mastoparan-S, followed by staining with SYTO 9 to detect live cells. Scale bar = 50 µm. Data are presented as mean ± SEM. Statistical significance was determined by unpaired two-tailed Student’s t -test (* p ≤ 0.05, ** p ≤ 0.01, *** p ≤ 0.001; nd, not detected)

Fig. 4 Analysis of the interaction between mastoparan-S and lipoteichoic acid (LTA) and lipopolysaccharide (LPS). A CD spectra of mastoparan-S (40 μM) in sodium phosphate buffer alone and in the presence of LTA or LPS. Antimicrobial activity of mastoparan-S against S. aureus and P. aeruginosa in the presence of increasing concentrations (0–64 μg/mL) of B LTA and C LPS. Data are presented as mean ± SEM

Fig. 6 Analysis of membrane integrity in S. aureus and P. aeruginosa following mastoparan-S treatment. Flow cytometric analysis of PI-positive cells, i.e., disruption of membrane integrity in A S. aureus and B P. aeruginosa . Planktonic cells of C S. aureus and D P. aeruginosa treated with mastoparan-S and stained with SYTO 9 (green-live cells) and PI (red-dead cells). Fluorescence microscopy images indicate the viability of bacterial cells after peptide exposure. Scale bar = 50 µm
